scripted_harness.evidence: The harness ran two typed planner/worker turns, restarted the controller after turn one, and ran the full suite successfully (53 passed).

subscription_adapter_dogfood.turn_one_evidence: Codex inspected the controller and protocol and confirmed that TURN_CLAIMED event payloads omit lease tokens while active lease/idempotency storage retains the live token needed for a safe result submission.
subscription_adapter_dogfood.turn_two_evidence: Codex inspected the public MCP/CLI history paths and confirmed they use the redacted event projection; malformed MCP payloads returned field-specific JSON-RPC validation errors.
manual_interventions_required: Planner-side create, submit-instruction, and complete operations were explicitly initiated.
The subscription-backed worker command was explicitly launched twice.
No arbitrary ChatGPT thread continuation was available or claimed.
subscription_adapter_dogfood.worker_sandbox_limit: The read-only Codex sandbox could inspect source and directly validate MCP handler shapes, but could not initialize uv/pytest writable cache and temporary directories. The full suite was run separately in the outer development environment.

dogfood_revisions: An initial adapter attempt exposed an invalid Codex response schema with untyped array items; the adapter now uses typed text arrays for Codex-generated evidence, tests, and commands.

Review evidence exposed lease-token exposure in immutable event payloads, non-actionable MCP validation errors, and missing per-run instruction-ID uniqueness; each was fixed with regression tests before the final two-turn run.
boundary: The run proves the local typed state and subscription-backed Codex execution path. Planner continuation remains an explicit Level C action.
